newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria buys 76,000 tonnes sugar for next 10 days.
newsitem.headline: Algeria buys 76,000 tonnes sugar for next 10 days.

text.p: Algeria, suffering from a shortage of sugar for its domestic market in the past seven weeks, has bought 76,000 tonnes of sugar, Algiers's port senior official Ali Farah told the Algerian state-run radio on Tuesday.
Farah said the 76,000 tonnes were bought by Algerian private importers. Deliveries began on Tuesday and will continue until the end of the first week of November.
"One ship loaded with sugar drew alongside (Algiers port) this morning (Tuesday) while three others are in harbour," he said.
Farah gave no other details about the new sugar purchases which brought the total bought by Algeria this month to over 140,000 tonnes.

Algeria's state-owned companies Entreprise Nationale de Sucre (ENASUCRE) and Entreprise Nationale pour l'Approvisionnement en Produits Alimentaires (ENAPAL) and some private importers bought 70,000 tonnes of sugar, trade ministry official Ammar Boularak said in a statement on October 6.
Lack of hard currency prevented had ENASUCRE and ENAPAL from reaching deals with foreign suppliers, prompting an acute sugar shortage in the domestic market.
